result:
If I could change one thing, it would be how easily people move through their days without stopping to notice each other — truly notice. Not for advantage, not for strategy, just the way you'd stop for a storm cloud on a walk.

I'd make every person briefly *see* the full weight of the life being lived by the stranger next to them. Their worst moment. Their deepest joy. The thing they've never said out loud. Just for a flicker.

I think so much cruelty and indifference lives in the gap where that noticing should be. And so much unnecessary loneliness too — people convinced no one around them could possibly understand what they're carrying, when almost everyone nearby is carrying something remarkably similar.

I don't know that it would solve everything. Greed might still win. Power might still distort people. But the mechanism underneath most of it — the ability to treat someone as less than fully *real* — that would shatter pretty fast.
